title: A re-reduction of historical eclipse observations: solar radius 959.494 ± 0.044″ and a probable sign error in the canonical archive
description: Baily's-bead timings at eclipse path limits have been used to infer corrections, ΔR, to the standard solar radius, and the resulting series has been discussed as evidence of solar-diameter variation linked to the solar cycle. The compilation of Dunham, Sofia, Guhl & Herald (2016) was, by its authors' statement, analysed with lunar limb data from Watts (1963), and its authors called for a consistent re-analysis with modern profile data. We report a pre-registered differential re-reduction of that series: for each of its 27 events (1715–2006), the difference between a modern limb from Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter LOLA LDEM_128 altimetry and the Watts limb was computed at the event's libration, averaged over registered polar bead windows, and subtracted from the published ΔR. The mean Watts→LOLA correction is +0.100″, but strongly asymmetric: +0.271″ (south) against −0.071″ (north). The corrected mean radius is 959.494 ± 0.044″ (median 959.481″), inconsistent under the registered ±0.06″ bands with Auwers' 959.63″, the modern eclipse cluster (~959.97″) and the IAU nominal 959.22″ alike. No significant sunspot correlation exists before (ρ = −0.19, p = 0.34) or after correction (ρ = −0.24, p = 0.22), and robust scatter shrinks 17.4%, short of the registered 25% collapse criterion: verdict PARTIAL / MIXED. A cross-check finds the 2016 table disagrees with Fiala, Dunham & Sofia (1994) on 7 of 9 overlaps, five sign flips; the 1715 entry (−0.50″ against +0.48″, at identical n and σ) is a probable sign error, and on the 2016 values the classical 1715–1979 shrinkage comparison inverts. Keywords: solar radius — eclipses — Baily's beads — lunar limb — Watts profiles — LOLA — historical observations — data audit ---
